page: Amazon Web Services m8ib.xlarge is a general-purpose server profile built on Intel x86_64 hardware and managed by the AWS Nitro hypervisor. The system provides 4 dedicated virtual CPUs derived from 2 physical cores operating at 2 threads per core. Processor execution is clocked at 3.9 GHz, providing consistent single-threaded clock speed across dedicated compute resources without relying on burstable CPU credit mechanisms.

The instance includes 16.0 GB of system RAM, maintaining an even allocation of 4.0 GB of memory per core. Hardware acceleration is absent, with zero GPUs provisioned. Local disk storage is also not bundled, meaning workloads require network-attached storage volumes for file systems and non-ephemeral operational state. The network configuration provides a baseline throughput of 4 Gbps, while complimentary public IPv4 addressing is not supplied with the instance.

The 1:4 core-to-memory ratio balances execution throughput and memory capacity within a mid-tier resource footprint. Because physical storage is entirely externalized, overall throughput depends on cloud block store integration rather than fast local solid-state drives. This specification is suitable for balanced production environments, including mid-tier relational database engines, microservice clusters, background job processors, and corporate web application hosting.
description: Amazon Web Services m8ib.xlarge is a general-purpose virtual instance based on the x86_64 architecture and powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor. The instance features an Intel processor running at a clock speed of 3.9 GHz, configured with 4 dedicated virtual CPUs mapped across 2 physical execution cores via multithreading. It is equipped with 16.0 GB of system memory, maintaining a standard 1:4 compute-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB RAM per core. The server does not include bundled local storage or integrated GPU hardware, requiring attached remote block volumes for operational data persistence. Network traffic is provisioned with a baseline bandwidth of 4 Gbps, while public IPv4 addresses are not included by default. With balanced compute and memory capacity, m8ib.xlarge provides balanced resource density for containerized microservices, mid-sized relational database environments, backend application components, and general enterprise web services.
